sections.content:
You know the gerund for simultaneous physical actions from B1 Unit 2 (*Llegó corriendo*, *Volvimos cantando*), and from C1 Unit 2 the rule against the gerund of a later action (*gerundio de posterioridad*). At C1, writers and speakers use **figurative and idiomatic gerunds** to show attitude, evasiveness or method alongside the main action.

Notice how the gerund paints the speaker's stance in a single stroke: *Respondió esquivando la pregunta* (she answered while dodging the question), *Siguió hablando haciendo la vista gorda* (he kept talking while turning a blind eye), *Se retiró tirando la toalla* (he withdrew throwing in the towel), or *Sonrió fingiendo calma* (she smiled feigning calm).

As in C1 Unit 2, the gerund expresses an action that happens **at the same time as** or **just before** the main verb—avoid using it for a **later result** (*gerundio de posterioridad*). Write *Abrió el libro y encontró un marcapáginas*, not *Abrió el libro, encontrando después un marcapáginas*.

sections.title: Figurative gerunds of manner vs later result
rows: *Respondió esquivando el tema con una sonrisa.*
*Aceptó el retraso haciendo la vista gorda.*
*Cerró la libreta y dio por terminada la tertulia.*
Later result gerund (avoid in formal prose)
Avoid: *Salió de la librería, recordando horas después la nota.*

items.spanish: Escuchó el relato fingiendo indiferencia, aunque le interesaba muchísimo.
items.english: He listened to the story feigning indifference, although it interested him greatly.

items.spanish: Salió del apuro esquivando la trampa con un comentario oportuno.
items.english: She got out of the tight spot by dodging the trap with a timely remark.

items.spanish: A veces conviene avanzar haciendo la vista gorda ante detalles menores.
items.english: Sometimes it is best to move forward turning a blind eye to minor details.

items.spanish: Abrió la novela y descubrió un marcapáginas con una frase escrita a mano.
items.english: She opened the novel and discovered a bookmark with a handwritten sentence.

sections.content: Use the gerund for an action simultaneous with (or framing) the main verb; join a clearly later event with *y* + a conjugated verb instead of a trailing gerund.
